top_story: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport on 11 October and the more damaging 14 October attack on Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran mark a sharp escalation in Yemen’s regional spillover, showing an expanding ability to hit Saudi civilian and economic infrastructure deep inside the kingdom. The human cost of that war remains stark at sea: the 11 October capsize of a migrant boat off Djibouti, carrying people toward Yemen, exposed how conflict and poverty keep driving lethal movement along one of the region’s most dangerous routes. In Gaza, testimony published on 12 and 13 October from Israeli intelligence personnel and soldiers points to a prior policy shift that normalized civilian casualties and the killing of unarmed Palestinians, sharpening scrutiny of how operational doctrine translated into mass harm on the ground. Together, these developments show a regional security environment in which military logics are increasingly unmoored from civilian protection, deepening both immediate casualties and longer-term social trauma.
